description: Drafter local reduce, SwiGLU and residual tail kernels, fused gate|up matmul, and the drafter MLP matmuls off the fixed 8-wide grids (R2).

levers.name: WP6 F-F1 drafter local reduce
levers.reason: after the unchanged dim-0 all-gather, the drafter's four slices and three fp32 adds ((p0 + p1) + p2) + p3 become one launch (draft_reduce_tp), bit-identical

levers.name: WP6 F-F3a drafter SwiGLU and residual kernels
levers.reason: the MLP branch's nine-launch SwiGLU and four-launch residual tail become one launch each with every bf16 rounding point kept (draft_tail_tp), bit-identical

levers.name: WP6 F-F3c drafter fused gate|up matmul
levers.reason: the drafter's gate and up projections run as one matmul over a load-time [gate | up] weight and the tail kernel reads both halves in place (so the arm also sets QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_TAIL=1), bit-identical column for column

levers.name: WP6 R2 drafter matmuls on device-width grids
levers.reason: the drafter MLP branch's 1D matmuls change only their program grid, from the fixed 8-wide rectangle to rows as wide as the device's worker grid (same cores, same per-core columns, same in0_block_w), bit-identical

profiles.name: wp6
profiles.reason: all four WP6 levers together: the arm whose paired timing is read against the production control, after each lever has passed its audit

profiles.name: wp6-audit
profiles.reason: all four WP6 levers and all four audits on the production stack: every lever compared with the served composition on the device at the warm pass; not a timing arm

profiles.name: wp6-singles
profiles.reason: all four WP6 levers and their audits on the audited lean twin (QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_SINGLES_AUDIT=all, the verify audits): the draft-singles audit compares the batched quad draft with each user's own single draft in the same round

image_files.reason: shared flags, markers, core plans and the eager audit of the four levers
F-F1: the reduce launch, the dispatcher target of feature_collective_tp and draft_mlp_branch
JIT reader kernel of the reduce launch
JIT compute kernel of the reduce launch
JIT writer kernel shared by the reduce and tail launches
F-F3a: the SwiGLU and residual launches
JIT reader kernel of the tail launches
JIT compute kernel of the SwiGLU launch
JIT compute kernel of the residual launch
F-F3c: the fused gate|up weight layout, matmul hook and audit
R2: the device-width grid for the drafter matmuls and its audit
the offline judge of the four levers' markers (chains reached, leaks), the rig host's copy of the smoke table

notes: SEE docs/tp4-fusion-wp6.md. For WP0: verified in a scratch merge of this branch with tp4/fusion-1 (27ef2115) after make_fusion_profiles.py --write and make_fusion_jobs.py --write: every entry lands, every WP6 template parses through c2_serving_job.py with rc 0, and three one-line edits to shared tests are still needed, none of which the generators place: (1) test_tp4_closure_literals.py SERVED: add draft_reduce_tp draft_tail_tp draft_gateup_tp draft_mmgrid_tp draft_fusion_tp (draft_mlp_branch.py and feature_collective_tp.py import them lazily and flag-guarded, so a flags-off process never loads them; without the entries test_every_lazy_import_of_a_served_module_is_classified fails); (2) test_serving_image_copy_closure.py C2_ONLY_PLAIN_IMPORTS: add draft_gateup_tp.py draft_mmgrid_tp.py draft_reduce_tp.py draft_tail_tp.py (overlay-only modules that copied P8 modules import; the test counts the lazy imports as plain ones); (3) test_tp4_fusion_jobs.py PublicTests.test_the_pack_names_no_host_address_registry_or_home_path reads every entry of references/fusion-jobs with read_text, and WP6's own templates are in references/fusion-jobs/WP6/ (a subfolder, which make_fusion_jobs.py leaves alone): skip directories (if not path.is_file(): continue) or recurse. tp_addresses: nothing to add (feature_collective_tp.gather_add_projection is already the rebound name; it now dispatches on QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_REDUCE itself). wp6_fake_device.py is test support only: not an image file. The profiles wp6, wp6-audit and wp6-singles in profiles[] are the combined arms the templates in references/fusion-jobs/WP6/ use. For WP7 (draft_attention_branch.py, not touched here): three one-line hooks, each lazy and flag-guarded as in draft_mlp_branch.py: the gather at the end of the attention branch: gather = gather_add_projection if quad is None else quad.gather_add_projection; then, if os.environ.get('QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_REDUCE') == '1': import draft_reduce_tp; gather = draft_reduce_tp.choose(gather, quad, 'attention') (the quad's 64-row chains; a branch without a quad already reaches the dispatcher); the residual tail: output = draft_tail_tp.residual(operations, mesh, finished, hidden, retain, site='attention') in place of the two typecasts, add and typecast, under QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_TAIL=1; the wo projection's program grid: grid = draft_mmgrid_tp.grid_for(operations, mesh, value, weight, (8, 10), columns, rows, kernel, site='wo') under QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_MM_GRID=1 (v678: wo +21 percent on its fixed (8, 10) grid). Until those land the engaged line's chains=<n> reaches 5 per quad, not 10: draft_wp6_smoke.py --expect-chains says so. F-F4 (one 64-row drafter LM head) belongs to WP7's draft_shared_head_tp.py / quad_draft_tp.py (the two 32-row halves are quad_draft_tp.head_candidates) and is NOT done here. For WP10 / WP0: the fused commit's 80-core projection (fused_commit_tp.py, 92.8 -> 124.7 us on 13x10 in v678) has the same fixed-grid problem: draft_mmgrid_tp.wide_grid(mesh, cores) and program_config(...) are the one-line fix there, behind QWEN_FAST_DRAFT_MM_GRID, with the same audit helper; est. -0.26 ms per round. No lever here is tau-only (all four are bit-identical by construction and audited on the device), so there is no tau A/B template.
